I am 74 years old, and I have farmed this land for 40 years, so I do not want to make my work too complicated or too risky. I only have 5 mu, and my family has some off-farm work, so I will keep using the wheat-maize rotation on all 5 mu because it is the system I know and it fits my land and irrigation conditions. Since I have well irrigation, I will rely on it to protect yield in dry periods, but I still want to keep costs under control. For wheat, I will use improved seed rather than old saved seed because I want stable emergence and better yield, but I will not push fertilizer too hard because I do not want waste or lodging. I will till with rotary tillage because it is easier for me to manage than deep ploughing and gives me a workable seedbed. I will irrigate a few key times and spray only as needed, keeping operations simple.

For maize, I will also plant all 5 mu after wheat harvest, because that is the normal way I manage the land through the year. For maize, I would choose hybrid seed because maize responds well to it and I want dependable production from a small area. I will apply moderate fertilizer, with nitrogen a bit higher than wheat, and I will use fewer irrigations than wheat unless the season turns dry. I will keep pesticide use limited to practical field needs, not excessive spraying. Since I am older and labor is limited, I will choose a plan that is familiar, steady, and manageable, with the goal of getting a reliable harvest rather than chasing the highest possible output.
